articles.headline: Tottenham prodigy Luca Williams-Barnett, 18, signs new contract
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur's rising star Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new long-term contract, the club has confirmed.
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur's rising star Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new long-term contract, the club has confirmed. 

The 18-year-old made his first Premier League start in Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich on Saturday, scoring the opening goal and providing an assist for Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi likened the teenager to Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal after Williams-Barnett's dazzling display on his full debut. 

"This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start," Williams-Barnett said in a statement.

"Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long -- it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

"The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that."

- Luca Williams-Barnett fell for under-21s joke before stellar Tottenham debut

- Tottenham's De Zerbi likens Williams-Barnett to Yamal after star stunning full debut

In our early matches, we have Bodø/Glimt taking on LASK, and Aston Villa in Istanbul taking on Galatasaray. Also on the schedule: Como vs. AEK Athens, Feyenoord vs. FC Porto, RB Leipzig vs. Lens and Slovan Bratislava vs. Real Betis.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL playoff picture: AFC, NFC seed projections, chances to make postseason
articles.description: We're looking ahead to how the 14-team playoff picture could line up -- and who will win divisions -- en route to the Super Bowl.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is past the midway mark, and we're tracking the playoff picture and the road to Super Bowl LXI. Which teams have the best chances to make the 14-team postseason field? Which have a lot of work to do to ultimately get in?

We used ESPN's Football Power Index to project the rest of the season, looking at the playoff picture for both conferences. We included updated odds for every team to make the postseason, clinch its division and even make the Super Bowl in February. Plus, we also have the FPI's projections for every game on the upcoming slate and how a win -- or a loss -- might impact each team's playoff chances, independent of other results.

Here's everything you need to know about the playoff picture right now, including which teams are trending up and down in each conference.

Jump to:

AFC picture | NFC picture

Game stakes

Trending up in AFC after Week 11: Houston Texans

Houston's FPI playoff odds jumped roughly 20 percentage points from last week following a Thursday night win over the Colts. The Texans are getting stellar play from quarterback C.J. Stroud, who is on a five-game streak with multiple touchdown passes. Though they have improbable odds to steal the AFC South title from the Jaguars, FPI has the Texans neck-and-neck with Pittsburgh and Cleveland for the final two seeds in the AFC playoffs. Houston lost to the Browns in Week 10, but it has a chance to beat the Steelers in Week 13.

Trending down in AFC after Week 11: Pittsburgh Steelers

Heading into Week 10, the Steelers had an 19.7% chance of winning the AFC North. After back-to-back losses, they're down to roughly 5%. What was most concerning about Sunday's loss to the Eagles? At 42, quarterback Aaron Rodgers became the second-oldest player in NFL history to lead his team in rushing yards, per ESPN Research. And Pittsburgh has three tough defenses up next (the Broncos, Texans and Jaguars -- all ranking in the top-15 of defensive EPA).

Trending up in NFC after Week 11: San Francisco 49ers

The 49ers are looking good for the NFC's No. 1 seed after their massive win over the Vikings in Mexico City. Quarterback Brock Purdy played his second-best game of 2026 by Total QBR (98.6), which is the third-highest performance in the NFL this season. After having a 65.1% chance at the No. 1 seed before Week 11, the 49ers are now over 80%. And they could all but secure the NFC West title with a win over the Seahawks in Week 12.

Trending down in NFC after Week 11: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Bucs had the second-best FPI odds out of any NFC team to win their division heading into Week 10 (63.9%), but they're down below 50% after back-to-back losses. A positive sign for the Bucs is that their Week 12 matchup is against the Panthers, who are currently two games ahead of the rest of the NFC South. Tampa Bay has won each of its past six home games against the Panthers, and it won 43-13 in Week 7.

articles.headline: Man United win appeal over Leny Yoro red card
articles.description: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
articles.body:
Manchester United have won their appeal over Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool.

The Frenchman was dismissed after eight minutes at Anfield after a challenge on Alexander Isak. On-field referee Sam Barrott decided Yoro had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity, a view backed up by VAR John Brooks.

United, who lost 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach, launched an appeal on Monday, insisting that Isak's heavy touch meant he would not have had the chance to score.

The Football Association announced on Tuesday that the claim of wrongful dismissal has been upheld and Yoro's one-match ban has been lifted.

A statement issued by the FA read: "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday Nov. 22."

Bruno Fernandes: Leny Yoro foul 'never a red card'

Bruno Fernandes told the BBC that it was "never a red card," adding: "I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."

Pochettino said: "I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control."

Kobbie Mainoo added: "The ball is already with the keeper when he's gone down, two players running at full speed. I mean, it's impossible to be a red, but it is what it is."

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola defended the referee's decision, saying: "[Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper."

It's the second major refereeing error in a game involving United this season. In September, referee's body Pro Ref apologised after Erling Haaland's goal at Old Trafford was mistakenly allowed to stand.

City, who were reduced to 10 men in the first half after Phil Foden's red card, won the game 1-0.

articles.headline: Lazio are top of Serie A despite playing without their fans
articles.description: Lazio's success this season has been one of the big stories in Serie A, made more remarkable by the fact that their fans won't attend home games until the club is sold.
articles.body:
We're approaching the end of November and Lazio are top of Serie A, with 32 points in 12 games. The last time it happened was more than 25 years ago and back then, soccer -- and Lazio -- were entirely different animals.

The Lazio team that would win the league in 1999-2000 was an expensively assembled super club -- so expensively assembled, in fact, that they'd go bankrupt a few seasons later. They boasted Siniša Mihajlović and Alessandro Nesta at the back, Juan Sebastián Verón, Diego Simeone and future Ballon d'Or winner Pavel Nedvěd in midfield, Marcelo Salas, Alen Bokšić and Simone Inzaghi up front. Coaching them was the late Sven-Göran Eriksson, who a year later would leverage the gig into the England job, becoming the Three Lions' first foreign manager.

The Lazio team doing it in 2026-27 are built on a shoestring, a function of an unpopular owner perennially accused of underinvestment. Still, they're a colorful -- if unremarkable -- bunch.

Their standout goalkeeper, Christos Mandas, is in his first full season at a starter, having played just 90 minutes of cup football last year. Right back Romano Floriani has a famous great-grandfather (Benito Mussolini), and an even more famous great-aunt (Sophia Loren). Their big summer signing, former Inter Milan super-sub Davide Frattesi (he made just 18 league starts in three seasons), has an influencer sister who dated Weston McKennie. Their playmaker, Reda Belahyane, started just six games in 18 months at the club before this year and was widely considered a bust until now. Their center back, Oliver Provstgaard, did win the Champions League in 2021 ... albeit the esports Champions League.

And then there's the manager, Gennaro Gattuso, last seen in charge of Italy's national team in April where he lost a do-or-die playoff to Bosnia-Herzegovina and denied the Azzurri a shot at the World Cup, a tournament nobody -- other than Brazil -- has won more times. Lazio is Gattuso's 11th job. None of his previous ones lasted more than two seasons, and his average tenure has been 41 weeks.

All this -- and Lazio's recent history of unremarkably finishing seventh, seventh and ninth -- would make their top spot an underdog story. But the remarkable part is that they're doing it with almost no home support after a fan boycott that began last January.

Lazio's fans feud with the owner

Lazio's average attendance through their first five home games has been around 10,000 spectators per game, a bleak number in the 70,000-seat cavern that is Rome's Stadio Olimpico. When you then consider that even that number is inflated by visiting supporters who often outnumber Lazio fans -- as happened for the visit of AC Milan in September, when the crowd was 21,000-strong -- you get a sense of how surreal the notion of "home support" is for these players.

For context, Lazio averaged around 44,000 a game in the two full seasons before the boycott, but season-ticket sales cratered from 29,918 in 2025-26 to less than 3,000 this y

articles.headline: NFL's international plan: More games, new TV deal incoming
articles.description: The NFL intends to play 10 international games next year, the maximum allowed under the CBA. It wants more.
articles.body:
Back in 2003, when the only NFL games played in other countries were preseason contests, it staged the American Bowl between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers at the Tokyo Dome. Leading up to the game, the Jets held a practice in the dome's outfield, where a 50-yard grid had been painted for the occasion. As soon as the practice ended, stadium workers scrubbed the grid from the turf so a baseball game could be played a few hours later. Just before the American Bowl kicked off later that week, stadium announcers offered attendees a brief lesson in the rules of the spectacle they were about to witness.

When the NFL returns to Tokyo, almost certainly in 2028, things will be very different. It will be for a regular-season game, perhaps in Tokyo's Olympic stadium, the changes in scale and professional sheen a reflection of the growth and ambition of the NFL's international push. What once felt like the circus coming to town, with the NFL dropping in on countries that had little existing interest, has morphed into a multipronged effort to make the NFL a global sport and to build an international fanbase from the ground up, complete with year-round flag football leagues, fan events and, of course, the games.

"Someone will be happy 20 years from now that we made this commitment and made a full run at being global," said Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president of club business, international and league events.

"Someone" is NFL owners, for whom international games are a way to reach what was, until recently, a largely untapped market for a sport that had been played almost exclusively in the United States. The host team is giving up the revenue it would normally make from ticket sales and game concessions (the league gives the host team a set payment instead), but the games have the potential to reap a far bigger return, perhaps soon. Eventually, the NFL will create international game packages and sell the lucrative rights to air the games domestically.

"Never forget international is just another media package," said one team executive. "International games give them more inventory."

Last Sunday, the NFL concluded its busiest international slate yet: nine games across four continents with games played for the first time in Rio, Paris and Melbourne.

Next year, the NFL intends to play 10 international games, the maximum allowed under the current collective bargaining agreement with players. The complete list of venues has not been announced, but the NFL had a great experience in Dublin in 2025, and one NFL source said a 2027 return there could be announced soon. Commissioner Roger Goodell has indicated that next year, the league wants to play multiple games in Germany -- one of its most popular international locations -- perhaps in Munich and Berlin.

The international game plan

Eventually, the NFL, with its eye on those rights packages, aims to play 16 international games. Every team would play an international game every year und

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: PSG eye Chelsea's Estêvão, Bayern's Luis Díaz amid injury woes
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain have added Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão to their shortlist. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão are on the shortlist of UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain, while Tottenham Hotspur winger Luca Williams-Barnett is being tracked by Chelsea. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Paris Saint-Germain have added Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão to their shortlist, as they consider whether to strengthen their forward line following the long-term injuries sustained by Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, according to Diario AS. PSG manager Luis Enrique wants to take time before making a decision, amid plans to assess the squad in the coming weeks, but the club have identified the 29-year-old Díaz as an option due to his direct dribbling style and Estêvão, 19, is also on the Ligue 1 club's radar due to his limited minutes in London.

- Chelsea are keeping tabs on Tottenham Hotspur winger Luca Williams-Barnett, who is closing in on signing a new contract, the Daily Telegraph reports. The Blues are watching the 18-year-old's situation alongside Borussia Dortmund, but Spurs are reportedly now handling the final details on an extension which could ward off interest in his signature. Williams-Barnett registered a goal and an assist on his first Premier League start in the 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday.

- Manchester United are preparing an approach for United States and Villarreal right back Alex Freeman, Football Insider reports. Scouts are reported to have been impressed by the 22-year-old's performances on multiple occasions, and the Red Devils have made him one of their top priorities for January in a move that would see him reunite with former USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino. Freeman has made 16 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season, continuing form since impressing at the 2026 World Cup in the summer.

- Arsenal and Newcastle United are monitoring Internazionale striker Pio Esposito, according to Nicolo Schira. The Serie A club are repored to have turned down approaches worth around €60 million for the 21-year-old, who is contracted until 2032, and viewed as an indispensable member of manager Cristian Chivu's squad. Esposito scored a hat trick in the 4-4 league draw with Atalanta on Sunday and was also on target in both of Italy's Nations League clashes this month, as he scored a brace in the 3-1 win over France on Nov. 12.

- Bayern Munich are considering an approach for New York Red Bulls striker Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, Sky Germany reports. The Bundesliga club are keen to acquire a short-term replacement for Harry Kane, who is set to be sidelined for several months following a ligament tear. Choupo-Moting, 37, is expected to be available as a free agent at the end of the year when his contract expires in Major League Soccer, and he is seen as a strong option due to his familiarity with the club. articles.headline: Fantasy football: Live Week 12 free agent pickups advice with ESPN expert
articles.description: ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody is here to answer your pressing questions live from noon to 1 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
With five NFL games to be played before we even get to the Sunday slate, Week 12 will certainly be one of this season's most unusual. The action kicks off with the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday (yes, Wednesday) night, so make sure you set your lineup early. The fantasy stars will be out in full force on Thursday as the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys play traditional host to Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles, respectively, while the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs provide the evening's entertainment. The Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers will play Friday.

As we monitor injury news, lineup usage and team matchups, you're going to want to move quick to set your lineups.  This is a good time to reserve your "flex" spots for the latest possible game times to give you the ability to make adjustments to your lineup come Sunday and Monday night.

You've got questions, ESPN Fantasy can help you find the answers. Our ESPN fantasy football expert will be here live from noon to 1 p.m. ET, just as he will be every Tuesday of the NFL's regular season, to try and answer all of your waiver wire questions and other fantasy-related queries. 

Which surprises from last weekend's games are worth picking up in your league? Should you drop the player that has disappointed you so far? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Eric Moody has answers.

He will do his best to try and answer as many questions as he can to get you and your fantasy team ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 12 free agent pickups | Week 12 rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.headline: Paris Saint-Germain drop one of this season's best kits in latest Jordan collab
articles.description: Three months into the season, Paris Saint-Germain finally unveiled their 2026-27 third kit in collaboration with the Jordan brand. It was worth the wait.
articles.body:
Reigning two-time UEFA Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain teamed up with Jordan brand, their long-time jersey collaborator, to create a stylish new third kit for the 2026-27 season.

The Ligue 1 giants have given their traditional jersey layout a contemporary overhaul, and the result is what you might expect for the club from the French capital of style.

- Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?

- DiBernardo joins Rapinoe, Pulisic in pantheon of great Olimpicos

- What soccer world was like when last GTA game was released

Thanks to the central "Hechter" stripe being present and correct, as it is on the Nike-branded home and away kits this season, the shirt is instantly recognizable as a PSG uniform. But the familiar design, which has been used since the club was founded in the mid-1970s, has been given an unusual and imaginative revamp to create something quite new and exciting.

Rather than simple block colors of red, white and blue, the iconic stripe is applied using a mottled tie-dye wash effect. Reds, greens and purples all swirl and merge together, providing contrast to the flat black base on which the shirt is built.

The PSG crest, Jordan's Jumpman logo and side panels are then all overlaid in bright red, while the names, numbers and sponsor marques are bright yellow -- creating pops of clashing primary colors that help liven things up even further.

With a little more in the way of creative freedom and abstract thinking, Les Parisiens tend to mix things up a bit when it comes to their Jordan kits. While it may have taken them four months into the season to unveil it, their latest collab is definitely worth the wait.

articles.headline: Jalen Green scores 25 and Devin Booker adds 22 to help the Suns top the Pelicans 123-119 in OT
articles.description: — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 123-119 in overtime on Monday night.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 123-119 in overtime on Monday night.


              Collin Gillespie scored five of his 18 points in overtime, and Miles Bridges had 13 points and 11 rebounds for Phoenix, which won its fourth straight game while handing New Orleans its fourth straight loss.


              Jordan Poole scored 28 points — all in the first three quarters — and Zion Williamson added 25 points for the Pelicans, who've dropped 10 of 11 since starting 4-4. 


              Saddiq Bey added 21 points and Jeremiah Fears had 11 assists for New Orleans. But Fears, who'd scored 29 points in a loss at San Antonio on Saturday, missed 14 of 17 shots against Phoenix. Trey Murphy also struggled as he works his way back from knee soreness that had sidelined him for seven of New Orleans' previous eight games. He shot 4 of 14 from the floor, and 1 of 6 from 3-point range. 


              The Suns pulled away for good with a 10-4 run during overtime that included Booker's jumper, Gillespie's layup as he was fouled and Bridges' 3.


              Phoenix also led 109-107 with 31 seconds left in regulation after Booker's step-back jumper. Fears' driving scoop tied it at 109 with 22.8 seconds left, and Herb Jones' steal of Booker's pass in the final seconds of the fourth quarter forced overtime.


              Poole, who scored 25 points two nights earlier in San Antonio, made his first nine shots against Phoenix, including six from 3-point range.


              He scored 17 in the first half, after which Phoenix led 56-54.


              Derik Queen scored 11 points for the Pelicans, but missed four of five free throws in the fourth quarter, when the Pelicans missed six of 12 from the line.


              Up next
              Suns: At Houston in NBA Cup West Group A play on Wednesday.


              Pelicans: At Los Angeles Clippers in NBA Cup West Group B play on Friday.

articles.headline: Kevin Durant scores 32 to power Rockets past Clippers 116-104
articles.description: — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.


              Houston led by six points with about three minutes remaining before Durant made consecutive 3-pointers to make it 109-97.


              Brandon Ingram made a basket for Los Angeles but an off-balance 3 by Durant seconds later put the Rockets up 112-99 with 1:30 remaining.


              Ingram made his debut with the Clippers after sitting out since May following surgery for a heel injury and to repair a partially torn Achilles tendon.


              The two-time All-Star joined the Clippers in September from Toronto as part of the trade for Kawhi Leonard. He missed the last two games of Toronto’s first-round playoff series against Cleveland because of the injury.


              He had 16 points and seven rebounds in 27 minutes.


              Darius Garland had 26 points and eight assists to lead the Clippers, who lost their fourth straight. Rui Hachimura added 19 points.


              The game was tied midway through the third quarter before the Rockets used a 9-0 run, capped by a 3 from Tari Eason, to make it 74-65. Houston led by 10 entering the fourth.


              Up next
              Clippers: Visit Memphis on Wednesday night.


              Rockets: Host Phoenix on Wednesday night.
